finding_details.closure: Each exact-resource identity group is processed as an explicit state machine: one canonical obligation is selected deterministically, it is executed, observed or claimed, exactly one canonical result is published, and every alias is classified from that exact result.  The published result carries the canonical obligation identity, the exact resource identity, attempted status, grant, settlement outcome, resource_outstanding after settlement, retention, the classified terminal state and the evidence publication generation.  DISCHARGED_BY_CANONICAL requires the same exact resource identity, complete publication, resource_outstanding false, a state that positively proves discharge, and no contradictory retention.  A canonical obligation that remains unresolved, is retained, receives no grant, raises before publication, or is concurrently claimed by another drain with no visible terminal result leaves its aliases retained under RETAINED_BECAUSE_THE_CANONICAL_OBLIGATION_FOR_THE_SAME_RESOURCE_DID_NOT_DISCHARGE_IT, which still spends no second settlement grant.
finding_details.defect: The drain identified an alias before the canonical obligation executed, and the classifier then prioritised alias_of over everything the canonical obligation actually did, emitting DISCHARGED_BY_THE_CANONICAL_OBLIGATION_FOR_THE_SAME_RESOURCE without proving that the canonical obligation had discharged the exact resource.
finding_details.evidence: Every drain row carries canonical_result; the drain ledger separates aliases_discharged_by_a_canonical_obligation from aliases_retained_pending_canonical and aliases_identified, and publishes canonical_results and per-row canonical_proved_discharge.
finding_details.invariant: An alias may be classified as discharged by its canonical obligation only after positive publication of a canonical result proving that the exact shared resource is no longer outstanding.  The existence of an alias relationship alone authorizes nothing.
finding_details.refusal_condition: DrainEvidenceContradiction, raised where the row is built.  The guard refuses DISCHARGED_BY_CANONICAL over an outstanding resource, and refuses a discharge whose named canonical result is missing, unpublished, for a different exact identity, itself outstanding, or in a non-terminal state.
finding_details.reproduction: Two obligations naming one exact owned cgroup, with the canonical settlement left unresolved: canonical attempted=true state=UNRESOLVED_AND_RETAINED resource_outstanding=true retained=true; alias attempted=false state=DISCHARGED_BY_THE_CANONICAL_OBLIGATION_FOR_THE_SAME_RESOURCE resource_outstanding=true retained=true.  A false cleanup claim over a resource that was still standing.
finding_details.title: canonical-result-dependent alias discharge

finding_details.closure: Inside the exact registry critical section, before the counter, the generation, the entry, the handle or the token is touched: if reservation is None and self._held_locked() >= CLEANUP_REGISTRY_CAPACITY, CleanupRegistrySaturated is raised.  No check is performed outside the lock, no capacity is reserved after insertion, and the existing atomic reservation-conversion path is unchanged.
finding_details.defect: The registry defines held capacity as entries plus live reservations, and reserve(), saturated() and require_capacity() all enforce that, but a reservation-less record() checked len(entries) alone.
finding_details.evidence: The saturation detail names retained entries and outstanding reservations separately; the registry evidence publishes retained, reserved, held, capacity and saturated together.  A refusal consumes no registry capacity and mutates nothing.
finding_details.invariant: At every externally visible state, len(entries) + len(live_reservations) <= CLEANUP_REGISTRY_CAPACITY.  Every reservation and every insertion, including reservation-less direct insertion, uses the same combined accounting under one lock.
finding_details.refusal_condition: CleanupRegistrySaturated, raised before any side effect.  An effect whose capacity cannot be reserved is never created, so the obligation this process could not retain is never brought into existence.
finding_details.reproduction: At capacity one: take one reservation, then call record() with reservation=None.  reserved=1 retained=1 held=2 capacity=1.
finding_details.title: combined capacity gate for reservation-less insertion

finding_details.closure: The preferred resolution is taken: probe creation acquires the same process-wide parent mutation boundary and holds it across parent identity verification, the collision check, the creation, the created-object identity capture and the immediate rollback of a partial creation, before releasing.  A parent whose identity cannot be read yields no boundary and the probe is refused rather than created outside the declared TCB.  The declaration is unchanged because the code now supports it.
finding_details.deadlock_analysis: One re-entrant lock per parent identity.  The probe-creation section acquires exactly one domain and nests no other acquisition; the manager-leaf boundary is entered and released inside initialize_cgroup_topology before probe creation begins; probe removal re-enters the same domain on the same thread re-entrantly.  No two domains are ever held at once by this path, so no lock-order inversion exists.  The three controller-owned child namespaces -- admissible-manager, admissible-effect- and admissible-probe- -- are disjoint, so no same-name cross-class collision is possible.
finding_details.defect: CGROUP_MUTATION_TCB declares every controller-owned child creation, rename, replacement, removal and final removal under a delegated parent serialized by one mutation boundary.  Effect creation, manager-leaf mutation, final removal and probe removal used that boundary; probe creation performed probe.mkdir(mode=0o700) outside it, so the declaration was broader than the code supported.
finding_details.evidence: CgroupDelegation.probe_creation records the mutation domain the creation held, whether it was held, and the identity of the object created.  cgroup_mutation_domains_evidence() continues to publish the exact bounded TCB and claims no atomicity against a hostile host.
finding_details.invariant: The declared trusted computing base is never broader than the code supports.
finding_details.refusal_condition: TOPOLOGY_EFFECT_CREATE_FAILED when the parent identity cannot be read or the parent was replaced between reading its identity and entering its boundary; TOPOLOGY_EFFECT_COLLISION when the name is already taken.  No probe is created outside the boundary in any of those cases.
finding_details.reproduction: At the instant probe_cgroup_delegation() created the probe, cgroup_mutation_boundary_held(parent_identity) was false, so a probe creation concurrent with an owned final removal under one delegated parent was not serialized.
finding_details.title: mutation-TCB coverage and description coherence

independent_audit_disposition: The independent audit of 6d687d4c778ae917f925da18aa89b2c53cdac911 refused final closure and forbade Milestone 3.  Its verdict and SHA-256 are recorded verbatim here and in the current validation report.  This report claims only that M2-B59, M2-B60, M2-M61 and M2-M62 are implemented and locally and physically qualified, pending independent audit.
known_limitations: The declared cgroup mutation boundary is a userspace lock over one process.  A mutation performed by a process outside this controller's trusted computing base is not excluded by it, and no atomicity is claimed against a hostile host; outside the boundary the code refuses, retains the obligation and classifies the refusal.

A canonical result published by another drain is read from a process-wide table.  It can only ever discharge an alias whose own evidence independently agrees that its exact resource is no longer outstanding, so a stale result cannot manufacture a discharge.
Independent acceptance of this closure is not claimed.  The independent audit of the starting commit refused final closure, and only that audit can lift it.
Installed-path qualification is not claimed.  Nothing here was run from an installed package.
Milestone 3 is not permitted and was not started.
